deploy.$comment: boot.py seeds the stores and then execs the API — it is not a wrapper that can be skipped. A startCommand of `python -m core.api.app` boots an API over an empty volume, because Kuzu is single-writer and the API holds the lock.
deploy.$timeout_comment: The FIRST boots after a data epoch do real work before the API binds, and it CANNOT be deferred: Kuzu is single-writer and the API holds the lock for as long as it serves, so there is no moment after startup when the graph can be filled. Measured on Railway at roughly 110 events/sec. After the 2006-2026 backfill the archive is ~1.5M events across three lenses, which is ~3.8 hours of merging against an hourly GDELT budget — so loading spans TWO OR THREE deploys by design, each resuming where the last stopped (scripts/boot.py). The window must also cover the ARCHIVE-WIDE RESCORE, which is the one step that cannot be resumed at all: it folds escalation per dyad across every era in a single pass, and an interrupted run leaves nothing behind. It waits until loading is complete and then needs hours (456,711 events took ~29min locally at ~262/sec). Hence 14400s: a LOADING boot wants ~9,600s (5400 GDELT + 3600 study + ~630 fixed) and a RESCORING boot ~12,000s (7800 rescore + 3600 study + fixed), and the window has to cover the larger. Note the window is a ceiling on PATIENCE, not a cost — a steady-state boot with nothing to load spends ~630s and binds immediately, so the only price of a generous window is that a genuinely broken boot takes longer to be declared broken. A window too SHORT is the expensive failure — it kills a container that was working, which is what happened on 2026-08-12 — and the cost of a long one is only that a genuinely broken boot takes longer to be declared broken.
